# PLAN — iteration 9
## Current state assessment
The verified incumbent is timing-feasible at 149 LUTs and 261 FFs; iteration 8 had the same resource counts and was rejected for no strict improvement. Iteration 7’s narrower product registers were also rejected, so avoid repeating those width changes. The seed preserves the known five-cycle top latency with `// @latency 5`.

## Hypothesis
Registering the saturated 16-bit result in stage 4 and forwarding it through stage 5 may remove one payload FF and simplify the final-stage logic without changing the five-slot handshake behavior.

## Instruction for generator
In `fir16_sym_core`, replace the 17-bit `rounded4` payload with a 16-bit stage-4 register holding the rounded and saturated result, and remove the stage-5 `result5` combinational logic. Keep stage 5’s registered `d5` update conditional on `ready5 && v4`, forwarding the stage-4 result; retain all valid-bit, history, reset, and hold behavior. Preserve the top interface and `// @latency 5`; compare routed LUT and FF counts and require all verification and timing gates.
